Threat intelligence plays a crucial role in identifying vulnerabilities, exploits, and emerging attack patterns. However, manual collection of threat intelligence from open platforms such as social media, security forums, and vulnerability databases is inefficient and error-prone, especially for students and early researchers. This paper presents a study on automated threat intelligence collection using open-source information while simultaneously assessing the security risks introduced by modern autonomous \\\"agentic AI\\\" frameworks. A detailed security analysis of an agentic framework commonly known as Open Claude (also referred to as Open Claw or Moltabot) is conducted to demonstrate how improper autonomy, lack of sandboxing, and uncontrolled third-party instruction execution can result in severe system compromise. The paper proposes a safer, restricted automation model and provides mitigation recommendations suitable for educational and research environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6316538\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.3366/e174418540800013x\", \"title\": [\"Book Reviews\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p> In 1925, a year central to the concerns of Advertising Tower, the short-lived short story writer Kajii Motojirô published a tale called ‘Lemon’. It has long been considered one the classics of Japanese short fiction. The climax of the story locates the focal character in one embodiment of Western-orientated Japanese modernity – the book section of Tokyo's Maruzen Department Store. The down-at-the-heel narrator has brought with him one shiny yellow lemon. He heaps up an armload of expensive, illustrated art books, sticks the lemon in the pile, and awaits the cataclysm. </jats:p><jats:p> William O. Gardener has looked back at the decade of the 1920s in Japan in this fascinating, sometimes frustrating, always informative study of how modernism in the arts and literature were generated within Japan's particular experience of cultural, social and political modernity. </jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.3366/e174418540800013x\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2007, 10]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "1bdc5cdef226e8abd7df5f7544f3ae92c7f3ef862d03ee70b85f9f1866298027", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.48009/3_iis_2026_102", "doi:10.3366/e1744185409000585", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6316538", "doi:10.3366/e174418540800013x"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.48009/3_iis_2026_102", "https://doi.org/10.3366/e1744185409000585", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6316538", "https://doi.org/10.3366/e174418540800013x"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=architectural+dimensions+of+communication+in+multi-agent+reinforcement+learning+and+coordination+stability&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1002/9781119699057.ch1\", \"title\": [\"Introduction\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/9781119699057.ch1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2020, 11, 6]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0006327305370545\", \"title\": [\"Multi-agent Coordination using Reinforcement Learning with a Relay Agent\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0006327305370545\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2017]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7589171\", \"title\": [\"Communication-Aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative UAV Swarm Coordination in Bushfire Monitoring\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Autonomous UAV swarms require effective coordination and structured information exchange when operating under partial observability and communication constraints. This study presents a communication-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, implemented as a CommNet–GAT fused variant of Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG), for collective coordination of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms in a simulated bushfire-monitoring task. The framework augments decentralised agent policies with range-constrained structured messages, CommNet-based neighbour aggregation, and an adaptive gating mechanism for fusing local and shared information. The approach is evaluated in a simulated partially observable disaster monitoring environment, using bushfire monitoring as a representative case study. The results show that explicit communication substantially improves cooperative fire detection, collision avoidance, and formation behaviour under the considered simulation conditions. The proposed fusion configuration achieved a fire-detection rate of 99.5\\\\% and reduced inter-agent and obstacle collisions relative to the no-communication configuration. Evaluation across a limited range of team sizes also indicated that the learned communication structure can be applied without changing the underlying actor architecture. These findings demonstrate the potential value of adaptive message fusion for communication-aware multi-agent coordination, while the results should be interpreted within the assumptions of the simplified two-dimensional simulation environment.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7589171\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1109/access.2023.3275883\", \"title\": [\"Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Based on Representational Communication for Large-Scale Traffic Signal Control\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2023.3275883\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2023]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "677040657576ee72dd4c1e0e60c0357686135b40f314cb290571eedd1f99f3f6", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "emergent_preferences", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1002/9781119699057.ch1", "doi:10.5220/0006327305370545", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7589171", "doi:10.1109/access.2023.3275883"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1002/9781119699057.ch1", "https://doi.org/10.5220/0006327305370545", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7589171", "https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2023.3275883"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
